content.text:
I couldn't read any files, so this diagnosis is inferred from the symptom and the usual layout of this NestJS auth boilerplate. I haven't confirmed it against the code.

Login and refresh succeed, so tokens are being issued. Every protected request fails, so the access-token check is rejecting those tokens. That points to a mismatch between how the access token is signed and how it is verified.

candidates.explanation: Most likely cause (inferred, not confirmed against the code). The strategy's secretOrKey or its validate() check does not match how access tokens are issued. For example, secretOrKey may read the wrong config key such as the refresh secret instead of auth.secret. Alternatively, validate() may reject the payload because it checks the wrong field (for example payload.userId instead of payload.id). Either way, every valid fresh access token gets a 401.

Access tokens are signed here. If the access token uses the wrong secret (such as the refresh secret), the wrong payload shape, or an already-expired expiresIn, the JWT strategy rejects it. Refresh still works because the refresh token is signed and verified consistently.
If the secret and expiry keys (secret, expires, refreshSecret) are mismatched or swapped in the config, the signing and verifying sides can disagree, producing 401 on all access-token requests.

fix.description: Make the strategy verify with the same secret used to sign access tokens: secretOrKey should be configService.getOrThrow('auth.secret', { infer: true }). Make validate() check the same payload field that getTokensData puts in the token (payload.id), and return the payload. Also check that getTokensData signs access tokens with auth.secret and auth.expires.
